chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar narrated from his brother Mūsā عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who is naked and the time for salat (prayer) has arrived, then he finds a garment, half of which has blood on it, or all of it. Should he pray in it, or should he pray naked? He said: If he finds water, he should wash it; and if he does not find water, he should pray in it and not pray naked.

key_terms.ثَوْبًا: a garment or piece of clothing
key_terms.دَمٌ: blood causing impurity on the garment
key_terms.صَلَّى فِيهِ: he should perform prayer while wearing it
key_terms.عُرْيَانٍ: naked, without clothing covering the body for prayer
key_terms.غَسَلَهُ: he should wash it, meaning cleanse the garment
key_terms.مَاءً: water used to wash the impurity

ai.seo_question: If a person only has a blood-stained garment and no water, should he pray in it or pray naked?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who lacks clothing at the time of salat (prayer) and only finds a blood-stained garment. It states that if water is available the garment should be washed, and if water is unavailable he should still pray wearing it rather than pray naked.
